opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions; Acquisitions and Collections; Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months) for exhibitions, catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, acquisitions and conservation. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply for Research and Travel grants only. Not for artists' personal practice.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and fund research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Applications are considered four times per year (Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer rounds). The Autumn round is currently open; future rounds open 1 Nov 2026 (Winter), 1 Feb 2027 (Spring), 1 May 2027 (Summer).

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); researchers whose interests lie in Henry Moore specifically (Studios & Gardens); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships allow artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's facilities in Leeds or Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round of applications will open in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation; plus publications to value of £50, copies added to Research Library, and publication of abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertation must relate directly to sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Henry Moore Institute awards two prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
